title: UI flickering in Hyper-V GPU-PV environments when sub-windows open (OpenGL Compatibility renderer)
body:
### Tested versions

-Reproducible in v4.7.dev (master, commit 1aaea38e7f)

### System information

Windows 11 in Hyper-V VM with GPU-PV (paravirtualized NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090), OpenGL API 3.3.0    NVIDIA 591.86 - Compatibility renderer

### Issue description

Severe UI flickering occurs in the Godot editor when running in a Hyper-V VM with GPU
   paravirtualization (GPU-PV). The main editor window renders fine, but as soon as any sub-window 
  opens
   (e.g., Create Project dialog, popups, file dialogs), all windows begin flickering/drawing black
   intermittently.
   
   In this environment, Vulkan device creation fails entirely (VK_ERROR_INITIALIZATION_FAILED), so the
   engine falls back to OpenGL Compatibility. With OpenGL, all windows share a single GL rendering
   context and wglMakeCurrent() switches between window HDCs. The GPU-PV driver struggles with this
   context switching, causing the flickering.
   
   Workaround: Running with --single-window eliminates the flickering completely, since all sub-windows
   are embedded in the main window and no wglMakeCurrent switching is needed.
   
   Other approaches tested (none resolved it):
   
   
    - DwmFlush() per-window and end-of-frame — no effect
    - Deferred SwapBuffers (render all viewports, then swap all) — no effect
    - Disabling vsync — no effect
    - Suppressing WM_ERASEBKGND — minimal improvement
    - Vulkan extension stripping/retry on vkCreateDevice — driver fails regardless of extensions

   Suggestion: Auto-detect GPU-PV environments (hypervisor detected + OpenGL active + Vulkan failed)     
  and
   automatically enable single-window/embedded sub-windows mode. Detection could use
   IsProcessorFeaturePresent(PF_VIRT_FIRMWARE_ENABLED) on Windows.

   Steps to reproduce:


    1. Set up a Hyper-V VM with GPU-PV (paravirtualized GPU sharing)
    2. Install Godot editor
    3. Launch the editor — main window renders fine
    4. Click "Create New Project" or open any dialog
    5. Observe severe flickering across all windows

### Steps to reproduce

1. Set up a Hyper-V VM with GPU-PV (paravirtualized GPU sharing)
2. Install Godot editor
3. Launch the editor — main window renders fine
4. Click "Create New Project" or open any dialog
5. Observe severe flickering across all windows

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

Minimal reproduction project is N/A — requires Hyper-V GPU-PV hardware environment.
